---
applyTo: "packages/genui/ui-judge/**/*"
---

Keep UI Judge a Rust-only screenshot and image-comparison crate. The default feature set is library-only; the `server` feature owns the `ui-judge-server` binary and HTTP adapter. GenUI Server owns all model evaluation, prompts, scores, and provider configuration. Do not add model dependencies, model environment variables, an interaction planner, an npm facade, or a JavaScript test suite to this crate.

Expose `capture_page`, `CapturePageRequest`, and `CapturePageError` for trusted page capture, and `compare_images`, `ReferenceImageComparison`, `VisualEvaluationError`, and `VisualEvaluationErrorCode` for deterministic image comparison. Keep runner objects, alignment internals, and fixture helpers private. The server feature may additionally expose its HTTP adapter.

Keep the feature-gated server protocol at `GET /health`, `POST /screenshot/template`, `POST /screenshot/lynxml`, `POST /screenshot/template/url`, `POST /screenshot/zip/upload`, `POST /screenshot/zip/url`, and `POST /compare`; do not restore the generic `POST /screenshot` route. Keep direct page navigation disabled. The JSON template screenshot route accepts only URL, global props, initial data, settle duration, and timeout. Download HTTP(S) templates through the shared SSRF-safe downloader, stage them at a server-selected path, and return a BMP from a fresh child process. Reject direct file URLs and all scoring or interaction fields. Trusted callers may use the library API for direct capture. Give every source-specific screenshot route a multipart/form-data POST body with required `entry` and optional `width`, `height`, `globalProps`, and `initData` parts. Reject query parameters, raw bodies, duplicate parts, and unknown parts. Accept `entry` as a safe relative staged path or equivalent `zip://` URL while never accepting a caller-supplied base directory, model option, or interaction step. The LynXML route takes a UTF-8 `source` part, the ZIP upload route takes archive bytes in `file`, and both remote-source routes take an HTTP(S) URL in `url`. Preserve the 8 KiB URL limit and a shared 10 MiB budget for all part contents, with at most 64 KiB extra multipart framing and one ten-second body-read deadline. Parse `globalProps` and `initData` as JSON objects and pass them through both ZIP and staged-source capture into the child page-load options; reject explicit `globalProps` for `.lynxml` entries because the native LynXML API cannot accept them. Keep page-data JSON in a private config file beside the child output, and pass only its path through argv so large multipart values do not exceed OS argument limits. Remote sources use the same SSRF-safe downloader and 10 MiB response limit. The shared downloader must reject credentials and non-HTTP(S) schemes, disable redirects and ambient proxies, validate every resolved address as public, and pin those validated addresses for the connection to prevent DNS rebinding. Resolve staged inputs through the headless resource fetcher against the internally injected canonical directory; do not duplicate its path policy in the HTTP adapter. Enforce the multipart byte budgets and total read deadline even when `Content-Length` is absent or false, then wait asynchronously for one of the four isolated-render slots before staging or extraction. Transfer the staging guard, requested internal URL, and render slot to a supervisor that starts one fresh `ui-judge-server` capture child for that source; on request cancellation or timeout, kill and reap the child before dropping the guard, and drain all supervisors during server shutdown. The comparison route accepts exactly one `referenceImage` and one `renderedImage` multipart upload, applies the existing image limits, and runs only deterministic normalization, alignment, and pixel comparison; it must not enqueue headless rendering. Read `LYNX_USE_PORT` with a default of `8080` and reject zero. Honor `LYNX_USE_HOST` when set by binding only its resolved IPv4 or IPv6 address; when it is unset, preserve separate IPv4 and IPv6 unspecified listeners. Have `build.rs` generate an executable `start.sh` in the Cargo profile output directory that starts the colocated `ui-judge-server` binary, copy the target Lynx runtime and `lynx_core.js` into the same runnable output layout, and package those generated assets rather than recovering them independently in `build.sh`. Obtain the default core script through the shared, SHA-256-verified artifact downloader rather than a checked-in fixture; honor `LYNX_CORE_JS_PATH` as a local build-time source while retaining the platform-standard packaged destination name. The server binary should select the packaged runtime when the caller has not set `LYNX_LIB_PATH` or `LYNX_SDK_DIR`, so the launcher stays a simple colocated executable wrapper. Accept HTTP connections concurrently, but run any trusted non-upload library page lifecycle sequentially through one process-wide capture broker whose dedicated owner thread reuses one `LynxContainer`. Untrusted staged-source capture is the deliberate exception: every request owns one short-lived child process and one container so Clay's process-global resource caches cannot cross tenants. Do not reintroduce a `LocalSet`, a `JoinSet` of ordinary capture futures, multiple long-lived production capture brokers, or multiple native container owners in one process. Use a bounded capture queue whose callers wait asynchronously for capacity within their request timeout, without blocking a Tokio worker. Do not reject requests merely because a capture or isolated-render queue is currently full; eager admission control and load shedding belong in outer middleware. Return `503` only when no live slot can become available because the worker is unavailable or shutting down. Limit request bodies and gracefully drain the HTTP server, all child supervisors, and the headless worker on SIGINT or SIGTERM. Treat a headless-worker panic as fatal: atomically stop admission, drop queued jobs so their handlers can drain, mark readiness unhealthy, initiate shutdown, and propagate the join failure from the server task.

Keep untrusted ZIP staging in the server-feature `src/zip/` module and never accept a client-supplied extraction directory. Reject uploads above 10 MiB before parsing, archives with more than 100 entries, overlapping entries, encryption, unsafe or duplicate paths, path/file collisions, symlinks and non-file/non-directory Unix types. Do not rely only on `ZipArchive::len()` for the count or duplicate checks: `zip` 8.6 stores entries by raw name and silently replaces exact duplicates, so also validate the structural central-directory entry count. Before constructing `ZipArchive`, accept only the rightmost classic EOCD whose comment ends exactly at EOF, reject ZIP64 sentinels and ZIP64 local or central extra fields, and structurally prove that the central directory ends at that EOCD with no more than 100 entries. Hide local headers and file data from the library's metadata fallback scan and reject extra EOCD signatures in the visible central-directory and comment region, so a malformed outer record cannot fall back to metadata embedded in an ordinary nested ZIP. Limit each file to 50 MiB, the archive output to 100 MiB, path depth to 20, components to 255 bytes, relative paths to 4096 bytes, and both declared and actually written compression ratios to 100:1. Extract through a fixed 64 KiB buffer into a fresh private `TempDir`, create files exclusively, count actual writes, propagate CRC/read failures, and remove the complete staging directory on every failure. Nested ZIP files remain ordinary files.

Run synchronous ZIP work through `spawn_blocking` with a separate four-permit semaphore and a ten-second absolute deadline. Wait asynchronously for an extraction permit within that same deadline; do not reserve extraction capacity in the HTTP adapter before buffering an upload. A timed-out blocking task cannot be forcibly stopped, so move its permit and temporary-directory guard into the blocking closure and check the same deadline between entries, reads, and writes; do not release capacity when only the async join wait times out. A successful `ExtractedZip` owns its staged-tree guard but not the shorter-lived extraction permit. ZIP-backed capture must inject the canonical base directory internally, acquire an isolated-render slot before extraction, and move the extraction guard and render slot into its one-shot child supervisor, which bounds staged trees and active renders to four. A full renderer or ordinary capture queue must leave the HTTP request future waiting until capacity or its deadline; rely on outer middleware for eager load shedding. Use a minimal child environment, null stdout and stderr, a private parent-liveness pipe on stdin, a private exclusive output file, and one absolute render deadline that also covers queue waiting, extraction, and output reading. Preserve the trusted temporary-volume variables and coverage profile variable without forwarding model credentials. Cancellation and timeout must kill and positively reap the child before releasing staging capacity, while parent death must close the lifeline and terminate the child. Bound reaping by a short fixed grace; if process control still cannot confirm it, terminate the service without unwinding the staging guard or requesting a core dump, and rely on the service supervisor to restart it. Deployment must add the hard containment process isolation cannot provide: a non-root account, read-only root filesystem, disabled core dumps, cgroup/container CPU, memory, and process limits, and a dedicated `noexec,nosuid,nodev` temporary volume with an ephemeral-storage quota sized for four bounded extractions. Record only sanitized archive byte/entry/declared-size/actual-size/duration/outcome metrics plus a trusted job identity, never raw entry names or free-form tasks.

Return original uncompressed BMP bytes with `image/bmp` in screenshot responses. Preserve those bytes for deterministic comparison. GenUI Server converts captures to PNG before passing them to its model or storing them in Bench reports.

Keep deterministic image comparison available through the Rust `compare_images` API and multipart `POST /compare`. Accept uploaded image bytes, bound compressed size and decoded allocations, normalize and align the images, and produce block-based pixel differences and a PNG diff. Model evaluation remains independent in GenUI Server; image similarity and diffs must not affect its VLM rubric.

Preserve the former TypeScript reference-comparison semantics during migration work: successful alignment compares the overlap crop, fallback comparison normalizes both images to their minimum dimensions with fill-style resizing, and pixel distance compares all four raw RGBA channels. Penalizing non-overlap or premultiplying alpha is a separate metric change, not a migration cleanup. Run CPU-heavy post-capture image work, including normalization, alignment, and comparison, on a bounded Rayon pool off the async runtime. Keep a permit with each Rayon job until the CPU work actually ends, even if its async waiter is dropped, so cancelled requests cannot overbook the pool.

Use the existing headless runner navigation and software screenshot APIs without modifying or duplicating the runner. `capture_page` accepts only file, HTTP, or HTTPS URLs and rejects bare paths before native initialization. Keep the container and page lifecycle in the single-owner worker so capture is callable from any runtime. Do not add remote interaction, browsers, emulators, or devices.

Keep the library timeout on connection, queue waiting, and navigation. HTTP staged rendering uses one absolute deadline that includes slot acquisition, staging, child execution, and output reading.

Rust unit tests and the runtime-backed `headless_e2e` test require no model configuration or mock-response environment variables. Build the React fixture and capture and compare its real pixels on Linux and macOS. Test GenUI model evaluation with deterministic provider mocks in the GenUI Server test suite.

Keep score normalization, rubric dimensions, and weighted GEQI results in GenUI Server. Do not add result-file generation, a UI Judge PR-comment action, or a GitHub comment publishing workflow.

Keep concurrent-request coverage fixed-size and behavioral: submit four distinct fixture bundles concurrently through the production single-owner worker, validate each screenshot, and do not add duration, QPS, latency, or throughput assertions.

Keep the existing React Lynx fixture at `packages/genui/ui-judge/tests/fixtures/react`, because the unchanged headless runner reads that path. Build its `.lynx.bundle` into the ignored `.generated/` directory and never commit generated bundle binaries.
